questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I saw the exchange program in Seoul as a great opportunity to make the most of my stay abroad. I wanted to visit a destination that you can’t visit on a short vacation, but rather take advantage of the fact that I’d be spending several months in the same country. I’d also heard many exciting things about Seoul’s history, its food scene, and the opportunities to get out of the city and into nature.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The process through SKKU (the university I attended) went well. They were really good at sending out information at the beginning (e.g. during the application phase) but as the date of my stay approached, I felt there was a lack of clarity. Everything went fine, though.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Not much. I missed orientation day, maybe I could have received some information there.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Dormitory.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: Great cooking facilities, meal plans weren’t available at the dorm I stayed in.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Even though it's on campus it might not be exactly ON campus. That didn't bother me, since I then got to explore another area of town. It took me 20-30 minutes door to door to reach school, which was fine since Seoul is a gigantic city.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I don't remember the process in details. I just remember the sign up process for courses being quite confusing.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Email service.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Not very successful. I had to change my list of courses several times as the ones I had initially planed on taking were fully booked. In the end I ended up taking some interesting courses but I would have loved to just be able to take the courses I had already gotten approval for from KU.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make sure to sit by your computer when the registration for courses open, otherwise you might have a hard time getting the courses you want/have pre-approval for from KU.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: From my experience the level of courses was lower than at KU. What made it "harder" was the ongoing attendance status, midterms and hand-ins, which I'm not used to from danish universities.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: There is less trust in the individual in South Korea than in Denmark. The students are more seen as young adults than actual adults which influences the style of teaching a lot. Many of the teachers I had were also very happy to hear themselves speak :) without really engaging the students...

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
* The Philosophy of Technology
*Environment and History in East Asia 
*Mental Health Problems
*Artificial Intelligence and Human Rights
*Health and Urban Life Social Mechanisms Behind the Relationship Between Place and Health

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
*Health and Urban Life Social Mechanisms Behind the Relationship Between Place and Health
*Environment and History in East Asia

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Local health insurance.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Grocery shopping was more expensive, than I expected. When we cooked at home it was very simple meals. Instead, we ate out a lot which was fun and very affordable. On campus you can eat a good lunch for about 30 danish kroner?!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be good at keeping an eye out and you'll find loads of different options.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Tennis! Even though the courts aren't great it was a nice was of getting to know the local Koreans a bit better.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Busan and Jeju were my favorites. There are so many options in South Korea! But near Seoul there are many beautiful waking trails. We spent many weekends going on easy hiking day trips.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Quite easy. Seoul's culture seems quite close to Western culture, I would say.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Even though Koreans are very friendly they don't tend to speak that much to strangers/foreigners. I would try to join some of the clubs e.g. tennis.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The language barriers.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The people and the food! Especially the food scene in Seoul is very different from anything else I had experienced.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Please don't stress if you don't enroll in the courses you planned on. You'll find something else that's fun and at the end of the day you might not be doing exchange for academic purposes? :)
2. Be brave and do things you wouldn’t be doing at home. Join a new club, cook new food etc. etc.
3. Explore the city area by area. Seoul is a biiig city. So instead of wanting to see it all (and thereby wasting hours in public transportation), slow down and explore one (or two) areas a day.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: KU doesn’t give credits for taking Korean Language as a course at SKKU.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Exploring a very different culture in depth.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: It was a struggle not being able to communicate properly with the locals. It made me feel a bit rude and ignorant. I think I would have gotten more out of my experience if this was not the case, but you make it work. Koreans are very friendly and you come a long way with a good translator and a smile.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
